executionHistory.summary: Security round over the surface the five bug packets changed, derived from each packet's own commits rather than inherited; for this packet it is rltaxworkspace.js, lifetime-tax-strategy.config.json and lifetime-tax-strategy-lab.html. ONE FINDING IS RECORDED AGAINST THIS PACKET, F-SEC-01, severity medium, not fixed here by design. The bound this packet shipped covers the RESPONSE-HEADER phase only, not the body: loadJson at lifetime-tax-strategy-lab.html:5729-5752 calls window.clearTimeout(timer) in the fulfilment handler, which runs as soon as headers arrive, and only THEN calls response.json(), so the body is streamed with no bound at all. Executed proof, replicating that function's shape byte-for-byte against a local http server with a 1000ms bound: an origin that never sends headers is rejected with AbortError after 1005ms, which is this packet's fix working; an origin that sends 200 headers and then stalls the body mid-JSON was STILL PENDING after 6001ms, six times the bound, with no rejection; a well-behaved origin resolved in 2ms. That reproduces this packet's own stated symptom, a pack origin that accepts the request and never answers suspending the boot chain, on the body rather than on the headers. A second observation on the same field: rltaxworkspace.js:291 admits any finite packReadBoundMs above zero with no ceiling, so 2147483647 was admitted, which is about 24.8 days and is effectively no bound, and 2147483648 was also admitted although it exceeds a 32-bit signed timer; measured in this Node, a 2147483648ms timer fired after 1ms with a TimeoutOverflowWarning, so just past 2^31-1 the bound inverts from unbounded to instant-abort.
